problem: (a) Find all positive integers n for which 2^n - 1 is divisible by 7. (b) Prove that there is no positive integer n for which 2^n + 1 is divisible by 7.
reference: Since 2^3 = 8 ≡ 1 (mod 7), for n = 3k + r with r in {0, 1, 2} we have 2^n = (2^3)^k · 2^r ≡ 2^r (mod 7), i.e. 2^n ≡ 1, 2, 4 (mod 7) for r = 0, 1, 2. (a) 7 | 2^n - 1 iff 2^n ≡ 1 (mod 7) iff r = 0, i.e. iff n is a multiple of 3. (b) 2^n + 1 ≡ 2, 3, 5 (mod 7), never 0, so 7 never divides 2^n + 1.

items.name: residues of powers of 2
items.criteria: Proves that 2^n mod 7 is periodic with period 3 taking the values 1, 2, 4 (e.g. from 2^3 ≡ 1 mod 7 and writing n = 3k + r). Merely listing a few values without justifying the period earns at most 1.

items.name: part (a)
items.criteria: States the answer: exactly the multiples of 3, and justifies both directions (multiples of 3 work, other n do not).

items.name: part (b)
items.criteria: Proves that 2^n + 1 is never divisible by 7 for any positive integer n, e.g. because 2^n + 1 ≡ 2, 3 or 5 (mod 7). A proof covering only some n, or relying on unproved claims, earns at most 1.
